A wobbly chair
slides.before: "wooden chair back leg loose where it meets the seat, no visible screw" — 40 seconds, three rewrites, still wrong.
slides.after: You turn the chair over and ask what's loose.

slides.headline: A plant that looks unhappy
slides.before: "leaves yellow at edges brown in middle drooping" — every result is a different plant.

slides.headline: Two tins in a shop
slides.before: Search one brand. Search the other. Open two tabs. Compare on a phone in an aisle.

slides.headline: Describing is the hard part, and you were doing it for free
slides.body: Turning a thing you can see into words precise enough to search is real work. Hand that to the camera and the question gets short.

slides.headline: You can just say "no, the other one"
slides.body: It's still looking while you talk, so you correct it the way you'd correct a person stood next to you. No re-typing the whole question.

slides.headline: Stop describing things to your phone
